A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SplatAD study, with complete main text, equations, tables, figures, references and Appendices A–F. Textual and visual inspection supports reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original camera and lidar rendering experiments, reconstruction, pose extrapolation and ablations in Tables 1–5, plus supplementary qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative experiments in Tables 1–5 and qualitative results in the main paper and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Gaussian representation, camera and lidar rendering procedures, rolling-shutter compensation, decoders and optimization objectives.

E1.justification: Both evaluate camera and lidar novel-view synthesis on PandaSet, Argoverse2 and nuScenes, with the same PandaSet reconstruction and ego/actor pose-extrapolation scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same comparator sets drawn from UniSim, NeuRAD, PVG, Street Gaussians and OmniRe, including the same task-specific omissions.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F retain the same sequences, preprocessing, alternating-frame training/validation split, reconstruction protocol and evaluation metrics. Training budgets and baseline evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 5, pose-shift comparisons in Table 4, rolling-shutter and decoder examples, and supplementary qualitative comparisons are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain identical point-estimate and averaging practices. Neither reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 contain identical numerical results and rankings. Qualitative findings are retained; Figure 3 uses the same underlying images with only display adjustments.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(25), including the lidar-tiling mathematics and rolling-shutter derivations in Appendices A and D, are unchanged. No formal assumptions or mathematical reasoning are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about joint camera/lidar rendering with 3D Gaussian Splatting, rendering quality, efficiency and performance across three datasets.

C2.justification: The interpretations of rendering performance and ablations are unchanged. Section 5 retains the rigid-actor limitation and the same proposed directions involving human reconstruction and diffusion priors.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and access links are unchanged. Both specify 30,000 Adam steps on an NVIDIA A100 and retain the same Appendix B details and Table 6 learning rates.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical, preserving the same positioning relative to NeRF-based simulation and automotive Gaussian-splatting methods.

P1.justification: Maryam Fatemi's first-page affiliation changes from Zenseact and Chalmers to Zenseact only, and the arXiv version/date updates. Scientific prose, terminology and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 slightly adjusts label and inset placement and one inset crop while retaining the same images and caption. First-page author spacing also shifts; other figures, tables and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The affiliation update and small Figure 3 presentation adjustments do not materially change the paper's evidence or clarity. Methods, results, mathematical reasoning, limitations and reproducibility information, including the appendices, remain unchanged.
